'''Andreas Engel''' (6 October 1943 – 1 April 2026) was a Swiss [[Structural biology|structural biologist]] and co-founder of the [[Maurice Edmond Müller|Maurice E. Müller]] Institute for Structural Biology at the [[Biozentrum University of Basel|Biozentrum]] of the [[University of Basel]].

== Background ==
Engel studied physics and mathematics in [[Bern]] (PhD 1972) and at the [[Johns Hopkins University]], Baltimore. In 1974 he joined the Biozentrum Basel. In 1986, after work in industry, he became Professor for Structural Biology. Engel and [[Ueli Aebi]] established the Maurice E. Müller Institute for Structural Biology.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Müller SA, Engel A |title=Looking back at a quarter-century of research at the Maurice E. Müller Institute for Structural Biology |journal=J. Struct. Biol. |volume=177 |issue=1 |pages=3–13 |date=January 2012 |pmid=22115996 |doi=10.1016/j.jsb.2011.11.013}}</ref> After becoming professor emeritus in 2010,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/news-events/news/news-details/article/farewell-symposium-for-andreas-engel/ |title=Farewell Symposium for Andreas Engel |publisher=unibas.ch |date= |access-date=2015-10-15 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304074003/http://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/news-events/news/news-details/article/farewell-symposium-for-andreas-engel/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Engel joined the Case Western Reserve University, to build up the Cleveland Center for Membrane and Structural Biology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pharmacology.case.edu/department/faculty/primary/Pages%5Cengel.aspx |title=Case Western Reserve University, Department of Pharmacology |publisher=case.edu |access-date=2014-02-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228180917/http://pharmacology.case.edu/department/faculty/primary/Pages/engel.aspx |archive-date=2014-02-28 }}</ref> He worked at the Department of Bionanoscience,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tnw.tudelft.nl/en/about-faculty/departments/bionanoscience/people/scientific-staff/prof-andreas-engel/ |title=TU Delft, People Bionanoscience Department |publisher=tudelft.nl |access-date=2014-02-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140223123830/http://www.tnw.tudelft.nl/en/about-faculty/departments/bionanoscience/people/scientific-staff/prof-andreas-engel/ |archive-date=2014-02-23 }}</ref> part of the [[Kavli Institute of Nanoscience]] and [[Delft University of Technology|TU Delft]] until his retirement in 2018. 

Engel died in Basel on 1 April 2026, at the age of 82.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/news/detail/obituary-for-prof-andreas-engel-1943-2026|title=Obituary for Andreas Engel (1943–2026)|website=Bbiozentrum.unibas.ch}}</ref>

== Work ==
{{sources section|date=April 2026}}
Engel pioneered the application of [[scanning transmission electron microscopy]] (STEM) and [[atomic force microscopy]] (AFM) to image biomolecular complexes. Mass measurements using STEM, 2-dimensional crystallization of [[membrane proteins]], cryo-electron crystallography and AFM were applied to study the structure of [[supramolecular]] assemblies [5]. Gram negative and positive pathogens, as well as bacterial envelopes were analyzed. Fujiyoshi and Engel solved the structure of [[Aquaporin-1]] in collaboration with Agre.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Aquaporin water channels – from atomic structure to clinical medicine | doi=10.1113/jphysiol.2002.020818 | pmid=12096044 |volume=542 |issue=1 |journal=The Journal of Physiology |pages=3–16|pmc=2290382 |year = 2002|last1 = Agre|first1 = P.| last2=King | first2=L. S. | last3=Yasui | first3=M. | last4=Guggino | first4=W. B. | last5=Ottersen | first5=O. P. | last6=Fujiyoshi | first6=Y. | last7=Engel | first7=A. | last8=Nielsen | first8=S. }}</ref> Together with Palczewski Engel's team discovered the packing arrangement of rhodopsin in the retina.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pharmacology.cwru.edu/department/faculty/primary/pages/Palczewski/articles/sdarticle.pdf |title=Structure of the rhodopsin dimer: a working model for G-protein-coupled receptors |publisher=cwru.edu |access-date=2014-02-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221162109/http://pharmacology.cwru.edu/department/faculty/primary/pages/Palczewski/articles/sdarticle.pdf |archive-date=2014-02-21 }}</ref>
Engel developed the first curriculum in nanoscale sciences that attracted many young talents to the University of Basel. Similar programs have since been implemented in many top universities.

== Awards and honors ==
*1996 Elected Member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]]
*1999 Max Gruber Lecture, Groningen
*2006 Karl Friederich Bonhoeffer Lecture, Göttingen
*2006 Edmund de Rothschild Lecture, Paris
*2012 Doctor Medicine Honoris Causa, Aarhus University<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.au.dk/en/annualcelebration/tidligere-aarsfester/aarhusuniversitysannualcelebration/honorary-doctor-andreas-engel/ |title=Honorary Doctor Andreas Engel |publisher=au.dk |access-date=2014-02-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304192444/http://www.au.dk/en/annualcelebration/tidligere-aarsfester/aarhusuniversitysannualcelebration/honorary-doctor-andreas-engel/ |archive-date=2014-03-04 }}</ref>
